title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021. MEASUREMENTS: Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy. RESULTS: Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units.

title: Maintaining IV Patency Throughout Pharmacokinetic Studies Through a Needle-Free Blood Draw Device.
abstract: 8 8 9 Pharmacokinetic (PK) studies require temporally precise measurements of drug concentrations in biological matrices, most commonly whole blood or plasma. However, repeated venous sampling may increase participant burden and complicate PK-intensive study designs. Needle-free blood collection devices that access peripheral intravenous (IV) catheters may provide an alternative approach to repeated venipuncture while maintaining sampling schedules and specimen quality. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of integrating the PIVO Pro needle-free blood collection device into a PK-intensive human laboratory study of inhaled Δ-tetrahydrocannabinol (Δ-THC), Δ-THC, and placebo. Participants completed a screening visit and three dosing visits conducted in a university research facility equipped with a full-scale driving simulator. During each dosing visit, venous blood samples were collected at nine time points over approximately 8 h through an indwelling peripheral IV catheter using the PIVO device. All participants reported that study procedures, including blood collection, were acceptable. Approximately 40% of vascular access sites required replacement, most commonly within the first hour and typically associated with poor initial blood return. Despite slower flow compared with standard venipuncture, sampling was generally sufficient to maintain the PK sampling schedule. One mild adverse event related to vascular access (localized bruising) was observed. These findings demonstrate the operational feasibility of needle-free blood collection through indwelling IV catheters in a PK-intensive research protocol conducted outside a traditional clinical research unit. Further studies are warranted to compare analytical performance and access durability relative to conventional venous sampling approaches.

However, repeated venous sampling may increase participant burden and complicate PK-intensive study designs. Needle-free blood collection devices that access peripheral intravenous (IV) catheters may provide an alternative approach to repeated venipuncture while maintaining sampling schedules and specimen quality.

title: [The Heart Team as a multidisciplinary approach to the management of patients eligible for surgical and transcatheter treatment of aortic valve disease - Consensus document].
abstract: Aortic valve disease, particularly severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, represents a growing public health problem due to the aging population. The increasing complexity of managing this condition - driven by the evolution of surgical and transcatheter techniques and the expansion of treatment indications - requires a multidisciplinary organizational model capable of ensuring quality and safety of care. This consensus document, jointly developed by AGENAS and the leading Italian scientific societies involved in the management of valvular heart disease, defines the principles for the implementation and functioning of the Heart Team as a central element of the decision-making process for patients undergoing evaluation for surgical aortic valve replacement or transcatheter aortic valve implantation. The document describes the composition, responsibilities, and operational procedures of the Heart Team, highlighting the importance of multidisciplinary assessment, patient-tailored treatment, shared decision-making with the patient, and outcome monitoring. The aim is to promote a standardized organizational model across the country, aligned with the scientific evidence and the most recent international guidelines, thereby contributing to improved clinical outcomes and greater efficiency of the Italian National Health Service.

title: [Abdominal aortic aneurysms: diagnosis, risk stratification and treatment strategies].
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm is defined as a focal aortic dilation ≥3.0 cm in maximum diameter, with rupture-associated mortality approaching 80%. Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women. Endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) provides an early survival benefit, with 30-day mortality of 1.8% vs 4.3% for open repair in the EVAR-1 trial, and substantially comparable long-term outcomes up to 15 years of follow-up, at the cost of a 15-20% reintervention burden and the need for lifelong imaging surveillance. Accordingly, the 2024 European Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines consider EVAR as the preferred treatment in most patients with favorable anatomy, reserving open repair for young patients with long life expectancy, unfavorable anatomy and specific conditions such as connective tissue disease, inflammatory aneurysms, graft infection and failed previous endovascular repair. Treatment selection should be based on the integrated assessment of individual operative risk, aortic anatomy and life expectancy.

Anatomical classification identifies infrarenal (80%), juxtarenal, pararenal and suprarenal aneurysms. Operative thresholds are 5.5 cm in men and 5.0 cm in women.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Apixaban Thromboprophylaxis According to Baseline Chemotherapy Class in High-Risk Ambulatory Cancer Patients: A Post Hoc Analysis of the AVERT Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized. METHODS: We conducted a post hoc analysis stratified by chemotherapy class of the randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled AVERT trial comparing apixaban (2.5 mg twice daily) with placebo in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy. The primary efficacy outcome was VTE, and the primary safety outcome was clinically relevant bleeding (major or clinically relevant non major bleeding (CRNMB)) per ISTH criteria. A subgroup analysis compared platinum-based with non-platinum chemotherapy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CI), adjusted for age, sex, and study site. Treatment-by-platinum interaction terms were used to assess effect modification by platinum exposure. RESULTS: A total of 563 patients were included and categorized by one or more chemotherapy classes at randomization. Compared with placebo, apixaban appeared to reduce VTE in patients on platinum (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.16-0.57), taxane (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.23-0.75), taxane-platinum (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.12-0.68), topoisomerase inhibitor (HR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.53), and antimetabolite regimens (HR 0.25, 95% CI 0.12-0.54), without increased bleeding. Among placebo-treated patients, platinum-based chemotherapy was associated with a higher risk of VTE compared with non-platinum regimens (HR 2.25, 95% CI 1.48-3.42), whereas no statistically significant difference was observed among apixaban-treated patients. Treatment-by-platinum interaction testing did not demonstrate significant effect modification by platinum exposure. CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis, apixaban thromboprophylaxis was associated with reduced VTE across several chemotherapy regimens with generally acceptable safety outcomes. Patients receiving platinum-based chemotherapy may derive greater absolute benefit from thromboprophylaxis in the setting of higher underlying thrombotic risk.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in cancer patients. The AVERT trial showed apixaban thromboprophylaxis reduced VTE in intermediate-to-high-risk patients initiating chemotherapy. However, the efficacy and safety of apixaban according to baseline chemotherapy class remain incompletely characterized.

title: Artificial intelligence-based surrogate modeling of hemodynamic indicators in abdominal aortic aneurysms using computational fluid dynamics.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive dilatative disease of the abdominal aorta with high rupture-related mortality, emphasizing the need for early risk assessment. Conventional anatomical indicators, such as maximum diameter, are insufficient to characterize rupture risk, motivating the incorporation of hemodynamic parameters. Image-based CFD enables the estimation of these parameters but remains clinically limited by high computational cost and long processing times. To overcome these limitations, deep learning-based surrogate models such as MultiViewUNet have recently been proposed, though previous studies were constrained by relatively low spatial resolution and limited coverage of hemodynamic parameters. In this study, we propose MH-UNet, a multi-view, high-resolution surrogate modeling framework that extends the original MultiViewUNet to a higher input resolution and additional hemodynamic parameters. MH-UNet converts three-dimensional AAA geometries into two-dimensional images from multiple viewing angles and predicts TAWSS, OSI, RRT, and ECAP using data from 101 patients. Both single-inference and dual-inference strategies were implemented and compared. Single-inference consistently outperformed dual-inference across all parameters; the cascaded dual-inference scheme amplified errors through the nonlinear OSI and RRT formulations, resulting in negative R² values for OSI, RRT, and ECAP. Among the single-inference predictions, TAWSS was predicted most reliably (R² = 0.803), whereas OSI was the most challenging to predict. Agreement between single-inference predictions and CFD-derived results demonstrates the potential of MH-UNet as a rapid surrogate tool for estimating WSS-derived hemodynamic indices in AAA under fixed boundary conditions.

Conventional anatomical indicators, such as maximum diameter, are insufficient to characterize rupture risk, motivating the incorporation of hemodynamic parameters. Image-based CFD enables the estimation of these parameters but remains clinically limited by high computational cost and long processing times.

title: Emergency thoracoabdominal aortic repair: distal-first approach with two previous aortic repairs.
abstract: Thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair after prior endovascular intervention is among the most technically demanding procedures in aortic surgery. We present an emergency thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm repair in a 59-year-old man with a history of preoperative haemodialysis, previous frozen elephant trunk for acute type A aortic dissection, followed by thoracic endovascular stent graft, complicated by partial spinal cord ischaemia and a type Ib endoleak. He presented with chest pain, and imaging demonstrated a 74 mm descending thoracic aortic aneurysm with impending rupture features. Multidisciplinary consensus deemed further endovascular intervention unsuitable, necessitating emergency open repair. A distal-first approach was used to overcome the distal perfusion challenges imposed by chronic aortic dissection. Following infrarenal clamping and the distal anastomosis to a branched graft, left heart bypass was established through its sidearm. Sequential visceral perfusion was performed, followed by anastomosis of the right renal and coeliac arteries to the graft branches. The proximal anastomosis incorporated both frozen elephant trunk and thoracic endovascular aortic repair, reinforced with double Teflon strips. The intercostal arteries were reimplanted. After declamping and de-airing, the superior mesenteric and left renal arteries were anastomosed. Motor-evoked potentials and cerebral monitoring were preserved. The patient recovered well and was discharged home 5 weeks postoperatively with a patent repair on imaging.

He presented with chest pain, and imaging demonstrated a 74 mm descending thoracic aortic aneurysm with impending rupture features.

title: Benefits of surgical task trainers to complement training pathways for junctional haemorrhage control.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Junctional haemorrhage remains a recognised cause of preventable trauma mortality. Although uncommon in the United Kingdom, such injuries demand prompt haemorrhage control, open vascular exposure and temporary shunting. Opportunities to develop these skills during routine vascular training are limited. This study evaluated whether high-fidelity pulsatile bleeding simulation improved trainees' self-reported confidence in managing groin junctional haemorrhage. METHODS: A prospective pilot educational evaluation was undertaken during a South West Deanery vascular training day. Nine vascular surgery trainees (ST3-ST7) completed a simulation using the Trauma Simulation® Femoral Injury Groin Task Trainer, identifying the bleeding source, obtaining proximal and distal femoral control, and inserting a temporary shunt under pulsatile haemorrhage. Confidence across four procedural domains was rated on a 5-point Likert scale immediately before and after the exercise, and scores compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank testing. No objective performance assessment was undertaken. RESULTS: n p All nine trainees completed both questionnaires. Median confidence improved in all four domains, although whole-cohort changes were not statistically significant. Among junior trainees (ST3-ST6, = 6), improvements in haemorrhage management, proximal and distal vascular control, and shunt insertion were significant (all < 0.05). The three ST7 trainees showed smaller changes; the groups were not compared statistically. Participants highlighted the realism of pulsatile haemorrhage and the value of consultant-led debriefing. CONCLUSIONS: High-fidelity pulsatile bleeding simulation is feasible, was valued by trainees and may help address an experiential gap in UK vascular training. However, confidence is not competence, and objective performance measures are needed before wider curricular adoption.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Junctional haemorrhage remains a recognised cause of preventable trauma mortality. Although uncommon in the United Kingdom, such injuries demand prompt haemorrhage control, open vascular exposure and temporary shunting. Opportunities to develop these skills during routine vascular training are limited.

title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.
englishSummary: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage.

title: A re-tightening suture technique for hemostasis during aortic root remodeling in chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection.
abstract: We report a 45-year-old man with chronic DeBakey type II aortic dissection, a sinus of Valsalva aneurysm, and severe aortic regurgitation. His atopic dermatitis remained poorly controlled despite topical corticosteroids and injectable anti-inflammatory therapy and he occasionally experienced cutaneous bleeding from unconscious scratching during sleep. He therefore wished to avoid long-term anticoagulation. Valve-sparing root replacement using root remodeling with external annuloplasty was performed. Bleeding from the proximal continuous suture line was controlled using a re-tightening suture technique that lifted the bleeding point, facilitated placement of an additional mattress suture, and secured the redundant continuous suture under renewed tension. Postoperative imaging showed satisfactory root geometry and no residual aortic regurgitation. This technique may provide a simple and reproducible method for controlling difficult suture-line bleeding during root remodeling.

He therefore wished to avoid long-term anticoagulation.

title: Orthotopic heart transplantation associated with hemiarch reconstruction for advanced heart failure and chronic aortic dissection: a case report.
abstract: Concomitant orthotopic heart transplantation and aortic arch replacement are extremely rare, particularly in chronic Stanford type A dissection. A 43-year-old man with end-stage heart failure and chronic aortic dissection underwent combined orthotopic heart transplantation and hemiarch replacement. Because of concomitant liver donation, the donor inferior vena cava required pericardial patch reconstruction. Despite early right ventricular dysfunction requiring veno-arterial ECMO, the patient recovered completely and was discharged with preserved graft function. This case demonstrates the feasibility of a single-stage combined approach with excellent postoperative outcomes in carefully selected patients.

title: Development and Clinical Validation of a Stroke Risk Decision System for Patients With Carotid Artery Plaque Based on AI-Powered Handheld Ultrasound and Laboratory Markers.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to develop and validate a fusion model combining portable artificial intelligence (AI) ultrasound imaging with multidimensional laboratory data to stratify risk and support decision-making in patients with carotid plaque-related anterior circulation stroke, and to assess its predictive performance and clinical utility. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded. All participants completed the 180-day follow-up. The primary outcome was new-onset anterior circulation stroke or TIA, defined as focal neurological deficit > 24 h with CT/MRI-confirmed infarction, or transient (< 24 h) deficit without evidence of acute infarction on neuroimaging. Outcomes were adjudicated by two neurologists (attending or above), with a third for disagreements. Participants were classified into ACS group (n = 140) and non-ACS group (n = 499). Ultrasound features of carotid plaques and clinical laboratory data were compared between the two groups. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify factors associated with ACS, and a nomogram was constructed based on the regression model. Internal validation was conducted using the bootstrap method. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination (C-index and area under the curve [AUC]), calibration (calibration curves), and clinical utility (decision curve analysis [DCA] and clinical impact curves [CIC]). RESULTS: (1) Significant differences were observed between the two groups in history of hypertension, smoking, hyperlipidemia, stroke, and myocardial infarction (MI), as well as plasma triglyceride (TG), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), high-density lipoprotein (HDL) levels, carotid plaque thickness, plaque area, plaque echogenicity percentage, degree of carotid stenosis, plaque continuity score, and plaque mutability score (p < 0.05). No significant differences were found in sex, history of diabetes, total cholesterol (TC), plaque location, or plaque fibrous cap continuity analysis score (p > 0.05) (2) Multivariable logistic regression identified history of stroke, history of myocardial infarction, plaque thickness, LDL, and HDL as independent predictors of stroke. A nomogram based on these factors demonstrated good discrimination (C-index/AUC = 0.884), with a sensitivity of 84.29% and specificity of 72.55%, along with excellent calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test p = 0.250). Decision curve analysis showed superior net benefit across a range of risk thresholds compared with the null model, supporting a multi-threshold stratified intervention strategy. Notably, when the predicted risk exceeded 75%, the model's predictions closely aligned with observed outcomes. CONCLUSION: The stroke risk decision system developed using AI-powered handheld ultrasound and laboratory indicators demonstrates clinical applicability for early prediction of anterior circulation ischemic stroke and is particularly suitable for early screening and risk stratification of high-risk stroke populations in resource-limited settings.

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 639 patients with carotid plaque via AI-powered ultrasound at community health centers. Anterior circulation stroke (ACS)/transient ischemic attack (TIA) patients were excluded.

title: Arthroplasty After Hemophilia Gene Therapy: Perioperative Implications and Clinical Experience.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gene therapy can provide sustained endogenous factor VIII (FVIII) or factor IX (FIX) expression, creating a perioperative phenotype that differs from both conventionally treated severe hemophilia and routine arthroplasty patients. Evidence for major joint replacement after gene therapy remains limited. AIM: To synthesize current clinical evidence on arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy and define practical implications for hemostatic management, venous thromboembolism (VTE) prevention, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary planning. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE and reference lists were searched through September 2026 for direct arthroplasty reports, invasive-procedure studies after gene therapy, and current guidance relevant to surgery and thromboprophylaxis. RESULTS: Published evidence includes dedicated total knee and total hip arthroplasty reports, trial-level arthroplasty observations, and broader invasive-procedure datasets after valoctocogene roxaparvovec, etranacogene dezaparvovec, and fidanacogene elaparvovec. These data show that gene therapy may substantially reduce exogenous factor requirements, but they do not establish a validated FVIII or FIX threshold for arthroplasty. Current World Federation of Hemophilia guidance recommends achieving procedure-appropriate factor levels, with supplemental clotting factor concentrate when necessary. In patients whose factor activity has shifted toward mild-deficiency or nonhemophilic levels, standard arthroplasty VTE-prevention principles should not be withheld solely because of the historical diagnosis of hemophilia. CONCLUSION: Arthroplasty after hemophilia gene therapy should be managed as phenotype-based major surgery: procedure-appropriate hemostasis, immediate rescue-factor access, serial postoperative monitoring, and appropriately timed VTE prophylaxis remain essential.

Evidence for major joint replacement after gene therapy remains limited. title: Primary arteriovenous fistula functionality and complications in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease: A single-centre outcomes report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Native arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for long-term hemodialysis. Primary non-function and inadequate maturation remain clinically significant problems, and detailed single-centre outcome series contribute to the evidence base, particularly in patient populations with a high prevalence of comorbidities such as diabetes mellitus. AIM: To describe the recorded functionality categories and postoperative complication profile after primary AVF creation in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), and to identify baseline characteristics independently associated with an adverse functionality category. METHODS: This single-centre outcomes study prospectively collected data on 96 consecutive adults with stage 4-5 CKD who underwent primary native AVF creation during 2020-2021. The primary endpoint was a three-level ordered functionality category: non-functional (0), functional at 12 months (1), and functional at 36 months (2). RESULTS: p p p p Mean age was 65.8 ± 11.6 years; 60 patients (62.5%) were male. Forty-five patients (46.9%) had diabetes mellitus; 50 (52.1%) received a distal and 46 (47.9%) a proximal AVF. Twenty-two AVFs (22.9%) were non-functional, 27 (28.1%) were functional at 12 months, and 47 (49.0%) were functional at 36 months. In the adjusted binary logistic model, diabetes mellitus was strongly associated with primary non-function (adjusted OR 27.79, 95% CI 5.56-138.84; < 0.001), while proximal AVF location offered a prognostic advantage (adjusted OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.07-0.74; = 0.014). In the adjusted ordinal model, diabetes was associated with lower odds of a more favorable functionality category (adjusted OR 0.24, 95% CI 0.14-0.41; < 0.001), and proximal AVF location with higher odds (adjusted OR 2.71, 95% CI 1.62-4.55; < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Diabetes mellitus was the strongest baseline predictor of primary AVF non-function and adverse recorded functionality in this outcomes series. Proximal AVF location was independently associated with a more favorable functionality category.

title: Risk factors for venous thromboembolic events at 90 days in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care: a multicenter retrospective cohort study.
abstract: PURPOSE: Evidence regarding venous thromboembolism (VTE) risk in palliative care populations remains scarce, and current thromboprophylaxis recommendations are largely extrapolated from non-palliative oncology cohorts. This study aimed to determine the 90-day incidence of VTE and associated clinical risk factors in hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective cohort study included adults with advanced cancer enrolled in a palliative care program who were hospitalized between 2018 and 2024 at two tertiary care centers in Bogotá, Colombia. VTE incidence was calculated, and clinical risk factors were identified using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models. RESULTS: A total of 782 patients were included (mean age 61 years; 58.7% male). Withing 90 days of admission, 81 patients (10.3%) developed VTE, corresponding to an incidence density of 2.3 events per 1,000 patient-days. Pulmonary embolism accounted for 40.7% of VTE events. In the adjusted analysis, lung cancer was associated with an increased risk of VTE (HR 2.34; p = 0.010), whereas higher Karnofsky Performance Status was associated with a lower risk (HR 0.98; p = 0.020). Age, sex, body mass index, baseline hemoglobin, active anticancer treatment, and white blood cell count were not independently associated with VTE. Overall, 90-day mortality was 66.3%. CONCLUSION: VTE was a frequent complication among hospitalized patients with advanced cancer receiving palliative care. Lung cancer and poor functional status were independently associated with VTE, whereas traditional clinical predictors were not associated with VTE. These findings support individualized VTE risk assessment and highlight the need for future prospective studies evaluating thromboprophylaxis strategies in palliative care settings.

title: Physiological monitoring and physiology-informed strategies in cardiac arrest: current evidence and clinical translation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite advances in cardiac arrest management, survival with favorable neurological outcomes remains limited. Physiological monitoring may complement standardized resuscitation by providing real-time information about circulatory effectiveness, reversible causes, and treatment responses. However, whether physiology-guided interventions improve patient-centered outcomes remains uncertain. This narrative review examines the current evidence and clinical applicability of physiological monitoring during resuscitation, physiology-informed rescue strategies, and individualized post-cardiac arrest care. MAIN BODY: During cardiopulmonary resuscitation, invasive arterial pressure monitoring, waveform capnography, and echocardiography provide complementary information about the circulation generated by chest compressions and potential mechanisms of resuscitation failure. Although observational and experimental studies support their physiological relevance, no adult diastolic pressure target or pressure-guided vasopressor strategy has been validated to improve survival or neurological recovery. Recent randomized trials of transesophageal echocardiography have demonstrated physiological or procedural effects without establishing clinical benefit. Among rescue strategies, extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation has yielded inconsistent results across randomized trials, with potential benefits dependent on patient selection, intervention timing, and system capabilities. Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta has not improved clinical outcomes in randomized evaluation, while head-up resuscitation remains investigational. Following the return of spontaneous circulation, randomized trials have challenged the benefits of uniformly higher blood pressure and oxygenation targets, mild hypercapnia, and deeper or prolonged temperature control. Individualized approaches incorporating cerebral autoregulation, venous congestion, and cardiopulmonary physiology are physiologically appealing but lack prospective validation. CONCLUSION: Physiological assessment may complement established resuscitation algorithms by refining clinical decisions during and after cardiac arrest. However, improvements in physiological measurements should not be equated with improved patient outcomes. Future trials should determine whether predefined, physiology-guided treatment strategies improve survival and neurological recovery.

title: Survey of the human proteostasis network: translation, protein folding, and organelle-specific systems.
abstract: The condition of having a healthy, functional proteome is known as protein homeostasis, or proteostasis. Maintaining proteostasis is the province of the proteostasis network, which consists of the cellular components that regulate protein synthesis, folding, localization, and degradation. The proteostasis network is a fundamental functional unit in biology with relevance to many diseases. Despite its importance, the human proteostasis network has until now lacked a precise definition, limiting our ability to interrogate proteostasis, integrate multiomic datasets, compare results across studies, or model proteostasis dysfunction in disease. To address this limitation, we have operationally defined the human proteostasis network by providing a comprehensive, annotated, and manually curated list of its components classified into nine Branches based on their function and localization - cytonuclear proteostasis, ER proteostasis, mitochondrial proteostasis, nuclear proteostasis, proteostasis network regulation, translation, extracellular proteostasis, the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and the ubiquitin-proteasome system - which we present in a series of three manuscripts of which this is the first. Overall, the proteostasis network annotation encompasses 3,151 components described by 4,043 annotations. Here, we present the 1,190 components that make up the first seven of these Branches, which comprise the compartment-based proteostasis network (cytonuclear, ER, mitochondrial, nuclear, and extracellular proteostasis), proteostasis network regulation, and translation. These Branches include chaperones, folding enzymes, systems for trafficking proteins, organelle-specific degradation systems, and the cell's translation machinery. This work provides a framework that will facilitate insights into how proteostasis is preserved in health, lost in aging and disease, and how it could be restored through pharmacological intervention.

title: Who Gets Feedback? Predictors of Receiving Narrative Feedback in Vascular Surgery Entrustable Professional Activities.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Surgical residents and fellows require high-quality feedback to guide skill development. Entrustable professional activity (EPA) assessments allow for frequent feedback in all phases of care. However, feedback is optional. We sought to understand predictors of feedback provision in a national, multi-institutional study of EPA assessments. METHODS: EPA assessments were collected in the multi-institutional Vascular Surgery EPA Pilot in 2024. EPAs were rated on a scale of limited participation, direct supervision, indirect supervision and practice ready. Assessments included entrustment rating, postgraduate year (PGY), phase of care, and narrative feedback. Self-reported demographic information was collected. A mixed effects logistic regression was performed examining the effect of entrustment ratings, PGY, trainee and faculty gender and gender concordance, trainee underrepresented in medicine (URiM) identification, and phase of care on the probability of receiving narrative feedback. RESULTS: In total, 1,998 assessments were collected across 19 institutions (n=17 residencies, n=13 fellowships). Faculty submitted 983 assessments with 759 (77%) containing feedback. 58% of trainees were men, 54% white, and 65% of faculty were men. Phase of care, post-graduate year, faculty gender, trainee gender, faculty-trainee gender concordance, and URiM-identification were not associated with likelihood of feedback. However, higher entrustment ratings were associated with lower odds of receiving feedback (OR 2.76 [95% CI: 1.25-6.10]). CONCLUSION: In this national, multi-institutional study of vascular surgery EPA assessments, demographic characteristics were not associated with likelihood of receiving or giving feedback. However, higher performing trainees are less likely to receive feedback. This may limit high-performing trainees' ability to reach their full potential.

title: Sex-Based Outcomes After Carotid Artery Revascularization in Symptomatic Patients: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Sex-based differences in outcomes after carotid revascularization remain poorly defined in symptomatic patients. We aimed to compare short and long-term outcomes between men and women with symptomatic carotid artery disease who underwent carotid revascularization across a ten-year period in three stroke centers. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted on a consecutive series of cases between 2016 and 2026. Cases included patients presenting with stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), or amaurosis fugax attributable to ipsilateral carotid artery stenosis within six months prior carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), or transfemoral carotid artery stenting (TFCAS). Patients with prior neck radiation were excluded. Primary outcomes were stroke, TIA, myocardial infarction (MI), and death within 30 days. Secondary outcomes included long-term stroke, TIA, MI, death, restenosis, and reintervention. Both primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed individually and as a composite endpoint. To account for sex-based differences and vulnerable plaque feature burden, a 1:1 propensity score-matched (PSM) analysis was performed among patients with available magnetic resonance angiography with vessel wall imaging (MRA-VWI). RESULTS: A total of 822 procedures were performed (men: 571, 69.5%; women: 251, 30.5%) with a mean age of 73.2 ± 9.2 years. Procedure distribution was similar between groups (CEA: 69.4% vs 70.9%; TCAR: 6.1% vs 5.6%; TFCAS: 24.5% vs 23.5%, p=0.89). Demographics and comorbidities were otherwise comparable between groups. Women had higher total cholesterol (185.9 ± 50.1 vs 158.1 ± 43.4 mg/dL, p<0.01), HDL (56.8 ± 18.1 vs 45.9 ± 15.2 mg/dL, p<0.01), and LDL (101.5 ± 45.4 vs 86.3 ± 38.0 mg/dL, p<0.01); however, the LDL/HDL ratio was not significant. Medication regimens were similar between groups, except estrogen use, which was exclusive to women (4.0%, p<0.01). Symptom presentation was comparable for stroke (49.0% vs 48.6%, p=0.91), TIA (32.0% vs 33.5%, p=0.69), and amaurosis fugax (22.1% vs 20.7%, p=0.67). At 30 days, the composite of stroke, TIA, MI, and death was similar (4.2% vs 4.0%, p=0.88), with no statistically significant differences in ipsilateral stroke (2.5% vs 1.6%, p=0.61), TIA (0.7% vs 1.6%, p=0.23), MI (0.5% vs 0.0%, p=0.25), or mortality (0.5% vs 1.2%, p=0.30). On long-term follow-up at 3.3 ± 2.6 years, the composite outcomes remained comparable (24.2% vs 24.3%, p=0.97), as were ipsilateral stroke (3.7% vs 5.2%, p=0.32), TIA (5.1% vs 4.0%, p=0.50), MI (2.6% vs 3.6%, p=0.45), mortality (17.5% vs 19.1%, p=0.58), restenosis (4.9% vs 7.2%, p=0.19), and reintervention rates (2.5% vs 4.8%, p=0.08). In the PSM cohort (men: 91, women: 91, N=182), the 30-day (3.3% vs 2.2%, p=1.00) and long-term (34.1% vs 31.9%, p=0.88) composite outcome of stroke, TIA, MI and death were similar. Restenosis (4.4% vs 7.7%, p=0.54), and reintervention (1.1% vs 6.6%, p=0.12) were also not statistically significantly different between groups. CONCLUSION: No statistically significant sex-based differences were identified in 30-day or long-term outcomes after CEA, TCAR, or TFCAS across a ten-year period at three high-volume stroke centers. Furthermore, on propensity score matching of our highest risk patient population with vulnerable plaque features did not affect their short- and long-term outcomes.

title: Outcomes of single-branched TEVAR with cervical debranching for zone 0 and zone 1 aortic arch repair: A VQI analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Single-branched thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) combined with cervical debranching has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open aortic arch reconstruction for patients requiring zone 0 or zone 1 proximal seal. Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI). METHODS: The VQI TEVAR registry was queried to identify patients undergoing single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching. Patients were included if the proximal landing zone was 0 or 1 and distal disease was confined to zone 5 or more proximal. Chimney, fenestration, stented fenestration, custom-manufactured, and physician-modified repairs were excluded. The zone 0 cohort included patients undergoing innominate side-arm branch repair with left common carotid artery (LCCA) and left subclavian artery (LSA) bypass/transposition, whereas the zone 1 cohort included patients undergoing LCCA side-arm branch repair with LSA bypass/transposition. Outcomes were analyzed descriptively. RESULTS: Among 38,215 TEVAR procedures screened, 50 patients met study criteria, including 39 zone 0 and 11 zone 1 repairs. Mean age was 73.8±8.5 years for zone 0 and 71.7±12.3 years for zone 1 patients. Prior aortic surgery was common (61.5% vs. 45.5%). Aneurysm was the most frequent indication for repair (66.7% vs. 72.7%). Staged treatment was performed in 74.4% of zone 0 and 45.5% of zone 1 procedures. Median procedure time was 166 and 163 minutes, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all patients. with no conversions to open repair and no completion Type Ia or Ib endoleaks. Cerebrovascular events occurred in 2.6% of zone 0 and 18.2% of zone 1 patients, including stroke in 2.6% and 9.1%, respectively. Spinal cord ischemia occurred in one zone 0 patient (2.6%). Myocardial infarction and postoperative dialysis occurred in 10.3% and 5.1% of zone 0 patients, respectively, and in no zone 1 patients. Thirty-day mortality was 10.3% following zone 0 repair and 0% following zone 1 repair. CONCLUSIONS: Single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching was feasible in selected VQI patients undergoing zone 0 and zone 1 arch repair. Given the small sample size and limited event counts, these findings should be interpreted as descriptive early outcomes rather than evidence of comparative safety or superiority. Cerebrovascular complications remain an important concern after arch endovascular intervention.

Contemporary multicenter outcomes of this hybrid approach remain poorly defined. We evaluated procedural characteristics and perioperative outcomes of zone 0 and zone 1 single-branched arch TEVAR with cervical debranching using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI).

title: Localization of Non-Compressible Torso Hemorrhage with Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound: A Swine Model.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Non-compressible torso hemorrhage (NCTH) remains a leading cause of preventable death in civilian and military trauma. In settings without cross-sectional imaging, the Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) is used to detect hemoperitoneum but is limited in evaluating the retroperitoneum, is highly operator dependent, and cannot reliably localize bleeding. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) has demonstrated high sensitivity for solid organ pathology, but its role in detecting and localizing NCTH is not well defined. METHODS: NCTH was induced in 18 swine (70-90 kg) via laparoscopic solid organ injury or endovascular injury to an aortic branch vessel. Standard FAST and CEUS were performed pre- and post-injury in a non-randomized, paired fashion. Outcomes included successful visualization of contrast extravasation with accurate localization of hemorrhage and time to hemorrhage detection. RESULTS: Both CEUS and FAST detected hemoperitoneum in all cases. CEUS identified active contrast extravasation from solid organ and vascular injuries in 78% of cases and improved detection of low-volume hemoperitoneum. CEUS also detected hemorrhage in the retroperitoneum. Time to detection was similar between modalities. CONCLUSION: CEUS is a feasible adjunct to FAST for detecting and localizing NCTH. This swine model provides a reproducible platform for evaluating portable hemorrhage localization technologies in austere environments.

In settings without cross-sectional imaging, the Focused Assessment with Sonography in Trauma (FAST) is used to detect hemoperitoneum but is limited in evaluating the retroperitoneum, is highly operator dependent, and cannot reliably localize bleeding. Contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) has demonstrated high sensitivity for solid organ pathology, but its role in detecting and localizing NCTH is not well defined.

title: Venous Thromboembolism Reporting in Fusion-Positive NSCLC Treated with Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors: A Systematic Review of Safety Reporting and Protocol-Level Provisions in Phase I-IV Clinical Trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized. METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria. RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods. CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC.

title: Effects of prehospital blood pressure on 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prehospital blood pressure (BP) could influence cerebral circulation and outcomes in acute large vessel occlusion (LVO). We investigated the association between prehospital BP and 90-day functional outcomes and explored effect modification by endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: We analyzed 1,106 patients with acute LVO transported by emergency medical services between 2018 and 2024. Prehospital systolic BP (SBP, mmHg) measured at the scene was categorized into four groups: <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups. The primary outcome was a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2. Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-3 and hemorrhagic complications. Subgroup analyses for the primary outcome were also conducted. RESULTS: Mean age was 79 years, and 51% were male; 60% underwent EVT. The SBP <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups included 120, 403, 403, and 180 patients, respectively. Cardioembolic stroke was most common and decreased with increasing SBP. Compared with SBP <120 mmHg, SBP ≥180 mmHg was associated with lower odds of mRS 0-2 (adjusted OR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.22-0.84; p=0.01), with similar trends for mRS 0-3. This association was significant in EVT-treated patients but not in non-EVT patients (interaction p=0.007). Hemorrhagic complications were similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated prehospital SBP (≥180 mmHg) was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes in acute LVO, especially following EVT. These findings highlighted the potential clinical relevance of prehospital BP assessment in patients with LVO. Further investigation should be considered for prehospital BP status in addition to the in-hospital managements.

We investigated the association between prehospital BP and 90-day functional outcomes and explored effect modification by endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: We analyzed 1,106 patients with acute LVO transported by emergency medical services between 2018 and 2024.

title: Plasma proteomics enhances genetic risk prediction and biological understanding of venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: VTE Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and the third most common vascular cause of death globally. While clinical and genetic risk factors have improved VTE risk stratification, they do not fully capture underlying disease biology. We hypothesized that integrating large-scale plasma proteomics with a validated polygenic risk score (PRS) would reveal novel biological understanding and improve risk stratification. METHODS: VTE In 44,138 UK Biobank participants, we examined associations between PRSand 2,911 plasma proteins using multivariable linear regressions. We evaluated proteins as predictors of incident VTE using Cox regression models. We employed bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (cis-pQTLs) instruments and genome-wide association summary statistics to infer potential causality. A protein-based risk score (ProteinRS) was developed with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) logistic regression and compared against a clinical risk model. RESULTS: VTE PRSassociated with 265 proteins after false-discovery-rate correction (FDR < 0.01). Pathway enrichment analysis of these proteins highlighted cell adhesion, cell-junction organization, and transmembrane receptor signaling. Time-to-event analyses identified 354 proteins that predicted incident VTE (FDR < 0.01). MR implicated 14 proteins in potential causal pathways to VTE, while genetic liability to VTE affected the levels of 44 proteins. A 60-protein ProteinRS improved discrimination beyond clinical factors (area under the curve (AUC) 0.664 vs 0.647; P = 0.024). Participants above the 80th percentile of ProteinRS had a 49% higher hazard of VTE (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.49, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.17-1.90) and those below the 20th percentile had a 48% lower hazard (HR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79) relative to the 20-80th percentile. CONCLUSIONS: Integrating genetic and proteomics data uncovered molecular pathways that link genetic susceptibility to VTE, highlighted actionable protein targets, and modestly enhanced risk prediction. Plasma proteomics therefore holds promise for precision prevention of VTE.

While clinical and genetic risk factors have improved VTE risk stratification, they do not fully capture underlying disease biology. We hypothesized that integrating large-scale plasma proteomics with a validated polygenic risk score (PRS) would reveal novel biological understanding and improve risk stratification.

title: One-Year Outcomes and Additive Risk of Restenosis After Rotational Atherectomy Plus Drug-Coated Balloon Angioplasty for Calcified Femoropopliteal Lesions in a Japanese Population.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate 1-year clinical outcomes and identify predictors of restenosis after rotational atherectomy and drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty for calcified femoropopliteal lesions. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter, single-arm study included 241 patients (178 men [73.9%] and 63 women [26.1%]) treated with JETSTREAM atherectomy and DCB angioplasty at eight Japanese centers. Mean lesion length was 16.5 cm, 28.6% were chronic total occlusions, and 91.3% had PACSS grade 3/4 calcification. Primary patency was freedom from restenosis (duplex ultrasonography-derived peak systolic velocity ratio >2.4 or occlusion) and clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR). At 1 year, 220 patients (91.3%) completed follow-up. RESULTS: One-year primary patency and freedom from CD-TLR were 85.5% and 91.3%, respectively. Exploratory multivariable analysis identified hemodialysis (HR 2.70, 95% CI 1.27-5.77, P = 0.01), chronic total occlusion (HR 2.85, 95% CI 1.39-5.83, P < 0.01), prior endovascular therapy (HR 5.08, 95% CI 2.48-10.4, P < 0.01), and popliteal artery involvement (HR 3.62, 95% CI 1.76-7.46, P < 0.01) as independently associated with patency loss. Patency declined from 94.1% with ≤1 factor to 38.1% with ≥3 factors. Neither severe nor nodular calcifications were associated with patency loss. Among restenotic lesions, 54.8% were occlusive, and shorter than baseline lesions. Angiographic distal embolization occurred in 37.8% and remained unresolved in 3.3%. CONCLUSION: One-year primary patency was 85.5%. Exploratory analyses suggested an additive association between clinical and anatomical factors and loss of patency. These findings require confirmation given the single-arm design and limited number of patency-loss events.

title: "CLEAN-UP AV": A composite interventional technique for treating Perianastomotic Arteriovenous Fistula dysfunction with balloon angioplasty: A 10-year outcome analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate long-term outcomes of a standardized interventional protocol, CLEAN-UP AV, for managing perianastomotic segment (PAS) stenosis or occlusion in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs). METHODS: This retrospective single center focused PAS angioplasty cohort from a tertiary referral practice analyzed 553 AVF angioplasties performed in 457 patients over 10 years. The CLEAN-UP AV strategy incorporates: advanced Crossing techniques, Lumen gain with appropriate balloons, treatment of the Entire circuit, Anastomotic dilation via optimal Access, No residual waist, procedural Ultrasound guidance, and postprocedural Pharmacotherapy. Angioplasty was performed using either U or V configuration technique: U angioplasty referring to angioplasty performed from artery to vein or from vein to artery and V angioplasty referring to sequential balloon angioplasty of the arterial and venous segments, including the anastomosis. Technical and clinical success, primary and secondary patency, adverse events, and predictors of patency loss were assessed. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 94.4% of procedures. Kaplan-Meier estimated 1 to 5 year primary and secondary patency rates in technically successful cases were 78%, 70%, 62%, 61%, and 58% and 89%, 84%, 83%, 80%, and 80%, respectively. On multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis, radiocephalic fistula configuration was an independent predictor of superior primary and secondary patency while hypothyroidism and high-pressure balloon requirement were independently associated with inferior primary patency. Major adverse event rate was 1.6%. CONCLUSION: In this single-center retrospective cohort, angioplasty performed using the CLEAN-UP AV approach was associated with high technical success and favorable long-term primary and secondary patency for perianastomotic AVF dysfunction.

METHODS: This retrospective single center focused PAS angioplasty cohort from a tertiary referral practice analyzed 553 AVF angioplasties performed in 457 patients over 10 years. The CLEAN-UP AV strategy incorporates: advanced Crossing techniques, Lumen gain with appropriate balloons, treatment of the Entire circuit, Anastomotic dilation via optimal Access, No residual waist, procedural Ultrasound guidance, and postprocedural Pharmacotherapy.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of Hemodialysis Arteriovenous Fistula Dysfunction Using 2D-Ultrasound, Elastography, and Vector Flow Imaging.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the diagnostic value of multimodal ultrasound-including 2D-ultrasound, sound touch elastography (STE), and vector flow imaging (VFI)-for the identification of functional and biomechanical abnormalities indicative of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis or occlusion in hemodialysis patients. METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 37 hemodialysis patients with AVFs, divided into normal (n = 20) and dysfunction (n = 17) groups based on digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or clinical/ultrasound criteria. For the dysfunction group, AVF stenosis was defined as >50% luminal diameter reduction on DSA, and occlusion as complete absence of flow. For the normal group, dysfunction was excluded by clinical examination (thrill/bruit) and normal duplex parameters. All patients underwent 2D-ultrasound, STE, and VFI examinations. Key parameters measured included vessel diameter, elasticity (kPa), blood flow velocities, turbulence index, and wall shear stress (WSS). Statistical comparisons were made between groups. RESULTS: No significant differences were found in vessel diameter or intima status between groups. However, the stenosis/occlusion group exhibited significantly lower mean blood flow, peak systolic/end-diastolic velocities, and WSS, along with higher resistance index and vessel wall stiffness (STE-mean: 30.35 ± 11.65 vs. 20.7 ± 7.52 kPa, p < 0.01). VFI revealed reduced blood flow velocity, turbulence, and WSS in dysfunctional AVFs (all p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: Multimodal ultrasound integrating 2D-ultrasound, STE, and VFI provides a comprehensive assessment of AVF structure and function, detecting functional and biomechanical abnormalities associated with AVF stenosis or occlusion.

METHODS: This prospective study enrolled 37 hemodialysis patients with AVFs, divided into normal (n = 20) and dysfunction (n = 17) groups based on digital subtraction angiography (DSA) or clinical/ultrasound criteria. For the dysfunction group, AVF stenosis was defined as >50% luminal diameter reduction on DSA, and occlusion as complete absence of flow.

title: Neutrophil extracellular traps drive immunoinflammatory remodeling in abdominal aortic aneurysm: from inflammatory amplification to precision therapy.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a chronic vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall dilation, extracellular matrix degradation, and an increased risk of catastrophic rupture. Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration. In the AAA microenvironment, local inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbances, altered mechanical forces, and platelet activation collectively contribute to the induction of NETosis. Persistent NET formation promotes immunoinflammatory remodeling of the aortic wall by activating inflammatory sensing pathways, including TLR9, cGAS-STING, and NLRP3, modulating macrophage responses, inducing vascular smooth muscle cell ferroptosis and phenotypic switching, and exacerbating proteolytic degradation, oxidative injury, and immunothrombotic responses. During disease progression, NETs may transition from early drivers of inflammatory amplification to sustained regulators of vascular remodeling, while in advanced AAA they may synergize with intraluminal thrombus formation and structural destabilization to accelerate disease progression. Circulating NET-associated biomarkers represent promising candidates for complementing conventional imaging-based risk assessment; however, their specificity and predictive value require further validation. Therapeutic strategies targeting PAD4-mediated NET formation, the oxidative metabolic environment, NET-associated effector molecules, DNase I-mediated NET degradation, and nucleic acid sensing pathways have demonstrated potential in preclinical studies. This review systematically summarizes the emerging roles of NETs in AAA pathogenesis and discusses future precision strategies integrating biomarkers, multi-omics profiling, and imaging-based risk stratification with stage-specific therapeutic interventions.

title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: a competing-risk analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray's test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P<.001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P<.001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P=.002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P=.030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 1.12; 95% CI, 0.74-1.70), whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation during 2017-2020, with follow-up through March 2025.

title: Insulin Dependence Erodes the Cardiac and Survival Advantage of Asymptomatic Status After Carotid Revascularization.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent (IDDM) and non-insulin-dependent DM (NIDDM) with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid artery stenting (CAS), stratified by symptom status. METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed January 2005-January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. Endpoints were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs). RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) NIDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days there were 1,645 MIs, 2,051 ipsilateral strokes, 1,806 deaths, 3,626 strokes or deaths, and 5,029 MACE; at 1 year, 2,378, 2,924, 8,269, 10,750, and 12,646, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR 1.24), mortality (OR 1.19), and MACE (OR 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE OR 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P<0.001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR 1.54, P<0.001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR 1.05, P=0.41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR 1.19, P<0.001). Relative to CEA, TCAR and CAS were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR 2.10 and 1.93, respectively, P≤0.01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every endpoint. CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival endpoints, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable to symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent (IDDM) and non-insulin-dependent DM (NIDDM) with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy (CEA), transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), and carotid artery stenting (CAS), stratified by symptom status.

title: Femoral Artery Access Outcomes and Technical Considerations in Vascular Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures. METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access. Data were obtained from the global GEN-VEDS Natural History Study and a retrospective single center cohort. Demographics, genotype, procedural indication, access and closure techniques, access-related complications, and outcomes were abstracted from clinical record. Major access-related complications were defined as femoral artery dissection, pseudoaneurysm, rupture, or closure device failure requiring open operative repair. RESULTS: A total of 117 femoral artery access sites were used in 105 endovascular interventions among 60 patients between 1989 and 2025. Median age at intervention was 39 years, and 53.3% of patients were male. Among 99 procedures with known access modality, 84 were performed percutaneously and 15 involved planned open femoral exposure. Manual compression was used in 33 percutaneous access sites, with no major access-related complications. Percutaneous closure devices were used in 39 access sites; major complications occurred in 5 access sites across 5 procedures, all requiring unplanned surgical exposure and repair. One additional percutaneous access site required unplanned open repair for access-related arterial injury and external iliac artery dissection before any closure device was attempted. Of percutaneous closure device failures, Perclose ProGlide and Starclose had the highest rate of failure (18.8% and 33.3% respectively). Three of four affected patients had large amino acid substitutions or exon skip mutations; the remaining patient had a small amino acid substitution but underwent 16-Fr sheath placement. No access-related complications occurred after planned open exposure. CONCLUSIONS: Femoral artery access in VEDS requires deliberate individualized planning. In this cohort, manual compression for smaller-caliber access (<6 Fr) was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas major complications occurred predominantly following attempted percutaneous closure. Planned open exposure, despite use in procedures involving larger sheath sizes, was not associated with access-related complications and may warrant consideration in selected circumstances, including procedures requiring larger sheath sizes, known prior closure-related arterial injury, and high-risk genotypes.

title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly amid conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI. METHODS: We utilized the NIS (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. Our outcomes evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs. endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. Mann-Kendal trend tested monotonic temporal trends. RESULTS: trend trend trend trend trend trend An estimated 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations were included (mean age 69.7 years, 40.0% women, 69.5% White). Overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with reversal and steady rise thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations included revascularization (n=14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n=16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization decreased (p=0.016), while endovascular remained stable (p=0.368), and hospitalizations without revascularization increased (p=0.016) over time. Endovascular revascularization rates did rise among females, non-frail patients, and those presenting with rest pain (all p>0.05). Overall, in-hospital amputation (n=6,270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n=1,086 [2.3%]) remained stable (p>0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased most substantially among hospitalizations without revascularization (p=0.007). CONCLUSION: We provide contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. Relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings underscore the need for further investigation into optimal CLTI patient selection and coordinated integration of non-operative care, such as medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

title: Sex differences in quality of life and psychosocial outcomes among patients with lower extremity varicose veins.
abstract: p p p p p p p p p ObjectivesThis study aimed to analyze the effects of lower extremity varicose veins (LEVVs) on quality of life and psychosocial well-being with respect to sex.MethodsDemographic data were collected using a patient information form; psychological status, quality of life, and pain intensity were assessed with the Beck Depression Inventory, SF-36, and VAS, respectively.ResultsOf the 24 patients, 54.2% were male and 45.8% were female, with a mean age of 35.21 ± 11.40 years. Educational level and daily working hours differed significantly between sexes, with females having a higher educational level (= 0.014) and males reporting longer daily working hours (< 0.001). These findings represent unadjusted group differences and do not establish independent effects of biological sex. Significant sex differences were observed in quality of life domains, including vitality (= 0.003), social functioning (= 0.001), and emotional role difficulties (= 0.005), all of which were more adversely affected in females. Psychological status assessed by the Beck Depression Scale was also significantly worse in females (= 0.029). No significant sex differences were found in sports participation (= 0.247), with most males (84.6%) and females (63.6%) not engaging in physical activity. Pain intensity at rest (= 0.459) and during activity (= 0.809) did not differ significantly by sex; however, females more frequently reported higher VAS scores, while maximum activity-related pain was 7 in both groups.ConclusionLEVVs significantly impair quality of life and psychological well-being, with females showing greater deficits in vitality, social functioning, emotional role, and depressive symptoms than males. Although pain intensity did not differ significantly by sex, females reported higher perceived pain. These findings highlight the need for sex-specific management of lower extremity varicose veins that considers occupational and psychosocial factors.

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.
