title: Hemodynamic Analysis of a Repaired Ascending Aorta with Preserved Aortic Root.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the hemodynamic impact of restoring a normal sino-tubular junction (STJ) following a novel Hegar dilator-based procedure in patients undergoing root-sparing ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm (ATAA) repair using computational modeling. METHODS: We retrospectively selected an ATAA patient who underwent pre- and postoperative gated computed tomography angiography (CTA). We developed a novel workflow to segment the lumen, thick-walled aorta, and aortic valve from CTA images for subsequent blood flow analysis using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and fluid-structure interaction (FSI). Morphological and hemodynamic characteristics of the root were quantified and compared against those of a control subject. Sensitivity analyses were performed to evaluate the impact of graft properties, leaflet material parameters and heterogeneity, wall compliance, external tissue support, and solid domain annular boundary conditions. RESULTS: Both CFD and FSI results showed that the postoperative geometry reconstructed with a normal STJ profile reintroduces sinus vortices during peak systole, similar to the control subject, which were absent pre-surgery. Accounting for aortic valve leaflets in FSI studies yielded a similar spatial patterning of the high-velocity jet and wall shear stress compared to the CFD data. However, FSI resulted in substantially elevated velocities, time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS), and energy dissipation, likely due to the dynamically changing orifice area and differing profiles of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT). CONCLUSION: We demonstrated that restoring a normal sinus shape and STJ profile during ascending aortic repair may have potential hemodynamic benefits. The study also highlights the model's sensitivities, particularly the LVOT shape and leaflet morphology and mobility, and may assist planning STJ reconstruction to yield optimal hemodynamics before intervention.

title: Predicting Post-TEVAR Endoleaks: A Pre-operative Hemodynamic Risk Factor from Patient-Specific Fluid-Structure Interaction Simulations.
abstract: PURPOSE: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is a minimally invasive treatment for thoracic aortic pathologies, including thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA). Computational simulations can provide valuable insights into TEVAR outcomes and complications before intervention. This proof-of-concept study proposes a novel risk factor R as a potential predictor of post-TEVAR type I and III endoleaks (ELs) using pre-TEVAR hemodynamic data. METHODS: Fluid-structure interaction (FSI) computational simulations are performed in ten pre-TEVAR patient-specific TAA cases, with known follow-up TEVAR outcomes. Hemodynamic drag forces acting on the aortic wall are quantified and used to define R, which combines parallel and perpendicular drag force components with aortic tortuosity. The patient cohort is divided into a calibration set, used to associate specific R values with three different risk levels, and a test set, used to preliminarily assess the agreement between the predictions derived from R and the post-TEVAR follow-up outcomes. RESULTS: ≤ ≤ Based on the R values obtained for the calibration set, R0.33 is associated with low risk of EL formation, 0.33 < R0.67 with moderate risk, and R > 0.67 with high risk. Once it is applied to the test set, the risk factor is able to correctly identify a type I EL. CONCLUSION: The risk factor proposed in this work is capable of identifying all the EL cases analyzed. This study represents a preliminary attempt to determine whether pre-TEVAR hemodynamics can effectively predict post-TEVAR complications and therefore aid clinicians in the pre-operative planning.

title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Ascending Aortic Perivascular Adipose Tissue Radiomics for Short-Term Mortality After Surgical Repair of Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
abstract: The purpose of this study is to investigate whether radiomic features derived from ascending aortic perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) provide incremental prognostic value beyond conventional clinical predictors for predicting short-term mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD). In this retrospective multicenter study, 241 patients with ATAAD who underwent surgical repair were enrolled and divided into a training cohort (n = 180) and an external validation cohort (n = 61). Radiomic features were extracted from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) images of the ascending aortic PVAT extending from the sinotubular junction to the origin of the brachiocephalic trunk. The best-performing radiomics model was integrated with independent clinical predictors to develop a clinicoradiomics model. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, calibration, decision curve analysis, DeLong testing, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis. Age, neutrophil count, creatinine level, and maximum ascending aortic diameter were identified as independent predictors of 3-month postoperative mortality. The random forest algorithm achieved the best radiomics performance. The clinicoradiomics model achieved superior discrimination, with AUCs of 0.935 and 0.855 in the training and external validation cohorts, respectively, significantly outperforming both the clinical model and the radiomics model (all P < 0.05). SHAP analysis identified multiple PVAT radiomic features among the most influential predictors. Ascending aortic PVAT radiomics provides complementary prognostic information beyond conventional clinical predictors for short-term mortality after surgical repair of ATAAD. A clinicoradiomics model integrating PVAT radiomics with clinical variables improves postoperative risk prediction and may facilitate individualized risk stratification.

title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group. CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.

title: Safe prescribing in pregnancy: Medication considerations for people with spinal cord injury.
abstract: CONTEXT: Pregnancy among individuals with spinal cord injury (SCI) occurs at rates similar to the general population, yet reproductive care for this population remains underexamined. Pregnant individuals with SCI experience secondary complications including neurogenic bladder and bowel, spasticity, pain, venous thromboembolism (VTE), and autonomic dysreflexia that often require pharmacologic management. However, limited evidence exists regarding the safety of commonly prescribed medications during pregnancy, contributing to clinical uncertainty and disparities in maternal and fetal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: Synthesize literature on the safety of frequently used medications during pregnancy for individuals with SCI to develop a pragmatic tool to facilitate initial identification and discussion of medications that may be considered during pregnancy. METHODS: A multidisciplinary team identified medications commonly prescribed for secondary complications of SCI. A literature review was conducted using PubMed, UpToDate, Briggs' Pregnancy and Lactation Guide, and the NatMed Pro Database. Medications were categorized by indication, evaluated for safety during pregnancy, and assigned a consensus recommendation based on available evidence through iterative discussion among the authors. RESULTS: Several medications for SCI-related conditions appear generally safe during pregnancy, including polyethylene glycol, acetaminophen, selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, low-molecular-weight heparin, insulin, and vitamin supplementation. Other medications, including anticholinergics, gabapentinoids, and some spasticity agents, have limited or mixed safety data. CONCLUSION: Pharmacologic management of secondary complications during pregnancy in individuals with SCI requires shared decision-making with patients due to limited safety data, emphasizing the need for nonpharmacologic management when possible. This review provides a reference for clinicians and highlights the need for prospective research and disability-inclusive guidelines.

title: [Premature loss of a mature arteriovenous fistula after a single cannulation: Delayed diagnosis of a venous pseudoaneurysm].
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pseudoaneurysms of hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) usually occur after repeated puncture-related trauma. Their occurrence after a single cannulation is exceptional. CASE REPORT: A 64-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease secondary to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis associated with essential thrombocythemia was referred for initiation of hemodialysis. A left brachiobasilic AVF with basilic vein transposition, created six months earlier, showed excellent maturation on Doppler ultrasound. The first fistula cannulation, performed with the aim of using the AVF to initiate hemodialysis, was complicated by a large arm hematoma without any hemodynamic abnormality of the AVF, leading to temporary postponement of hemodialysis initiation to allow the fistula to rest. Five weeks later, when hemodialysis could no longer be deferred, the persistence of the hematoma precluded recannulation of the AVF; a tunneled central venous catheter was therefore placed on March 14, 2024. The following day, the patient experienced a sudden recurrence of pain and rapid swelling of the left arm. Doppler ultrasound revealed a 4.5 × 4.9 × 9.3 cm venous pseudoaneurysm arising from the transposed basilic vein. Surgical resection of the pseudoaneurysm with ligation of the AVF was required, resulting in permanent loss of the vascular access before it could be used for hemodialysis. CONCLUSION: This case highlights that a single difficult cannulation of a mature arteriovenous fistula may exceptionally lead to a delayed pseudoaneurysm and permanent loss of the vascular access, particularly in the presence of factors predisposing to bleeding complications.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Pseudoaneurysms of hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) usually occur after repeated puncture-related trauma. Their occurrence after a single cannulation is exceptional. CASE REPORT: A 64-year-old man with end-stage kidney disease secondary to focal segmental glomerulosclerosis associated with essential thrombocythemia was referred for initiation of hemodialysis.

title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment. INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals. RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.
englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery. INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD). RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT03121209.
englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.
englishSummary: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up.

title: Standardized Tool for Prophylaxis (SToP) of venous thromboembolism: An asynchronous curriculum to enhance venous thromboembolism prevention in pediatric inflammatory bowel disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Compared to those without inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), pediatric patients with IBD are at three- to sevenfold increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), a complication associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Despite this risk, gaps persist in clinician awareness, and standardized education and guidelines regarding prevention are lacking. We aimed to improve pediatric healthcare provider knowledge and confidence regarding VTE prevention in patients hospitalized with active IBD. METHODS: We created a three-module, online, asynchronous educational course. Using a pre-post survey design, we studied self-reported confidence and knowledge. Responses were measured using 5-point (confidence) and 3-point (knowledge) Likert scales, with higher scores reflecting greater confidence/knowledge. Post-course satisfaction was also measured. Change in confidence was analyzed using linear regression, and knowledge change using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: M M M p p p Sixty-five participants completed the course; 55% attending physicians, 71% female, 73% practiced in an academic setting. Mean () confidence in VTE prevention increased from pre- ( = 2.57, standard deviation [SD] = 0.98) to post-test ( = 4.07, SD = 0.60), < 0.001. Median (Md) knowledge also increased from the module one pre- (Md = 3.00, interquartile range [IQR] = 1.00) to post-test (Md = 3.00, IQR = 0.00), < 0.001, and module two pre- (Md = 2.00, IQR = 1.00) to post-test (Md = 3.00, IQR = 0.00), < 0.001. Participants reported high levels of satisfaction with the curriculum. CONCLUSIONS: A brief, asynchronous educational intervention significantly improved clinician knowledge and confidence in VTE prevention for pediatric patients hospitalized with active IBD. Scalable online curricula may represent an effective strategy to address educational gaps and support improved clinical care in high-risk populations.

Despite this risk, gaps persist in clinician awareness, and standardized education and guidelines regarding prevention are lacking. We aimed to improve pediatric healthcare provider knowledge and confidence regarding VTE prevention in patients hospitalized with active IBD.

title: Catheter-Induced Type B Aortic Dissection After TAVI: Delayed Adverse Remodeling.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Catheter-induced type B aortic dissection is a rare complication of transcatheter aortic valve implantation with uncertain long-term behavior. CASE SUMMARY: An 85-year-old woman developed a focal aortic isthmus dissection during transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Initial computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed no malperfusion or rupture; conservative management and serial CTA surveillance were selected. Despite persistent clinical stability, follow-up CTA demonstrated progressive focal outpouching and pseudoaneurysmal remodeling. At 17 months, elective thoracic endovascular aortic repair achieved complete exclusion of the lesion. DISCUSSION: Catheter-induced dissection may represent a mechanistically distinct entity from spontaneous type B aortic dissection, limiting direct extrapolation of conventional management pathways. Morphological progression, rather than symptoms or absolute aortic diameter, prompted intervention. TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Clinical stability does not establish aortic wall healing. Long-term serial CTA can identify silent adverse remodeling and guide elective thoracic endovascular aortic repair in selected patients.

Initial computed tomography angiography (CTA) showed no malperfusion or rupture; conservative management and serial CTA surveillance were selected.

title: Early Experience of Fiber Optic RealShape Technology in Endovascular Interventions for Peripheral Artery Disease: A Prospective Single-Center Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Interventions in peripheral artery disease (PAD) have changed significantly over the past decades. Most centers have adopted an endovascular-first strategy resulting in an increased radiation exposure, especially for the treatment team. Fiber Optic RealShape (FORS) technology uses laser light instead of fluoroscopy to visualize the specially designed guidewire and catheters. The aim of this early experience overview was to evaluate feasibility and safety of FORS-guided navigation for endovascular interventions in PAD. METHODS: This overview presents prospectively collected, single-center data of FORS-guided PAD interventions. Feasibility was evaluated through technical success in crossing stenotic lesion(s) or occlusion(s). Lesion characteristics were also recorded. Safety was assessed by scoring of intraoperative adverse events related to FORS. Secondary assessments included navigation time, and radiation exposure outcomes (cumulative air kerma [CAK], air kerma-area product [KAP], and fluoroscopy time [FT]) during crossing of the culprit lesion. RESULTS: In 22 patients (31 lesions) selected for FORS-guided PAD interventions, 22 of 31 lesions (71.0%) were successfully crossed while using FORS-enabled devices, without adverse events. Median length of the treated lesions was 48.0 mm (23.0-87.0). Sixteen lesions (51.6%) had a severe degree of stenosis and 10 lesions (32.3%) had a moderate degree of stenosis, defined according to the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial criteria. Navigation times, CAK, and FT were highest during FORS-guided interventions of most complex stenotic lesions. CONCLUSION: Fiber Optic RealShape-guided navigation and lesion crossing in PAD interventions is feasible and safe. Expansion of the FORS portfolio hypothetically in combination with other radiation-reducing technologies might enable a radiation-free interventional environment in the future.Clinical ImpactFiber Optic RealShape (FORS) represents a novel technology that enables visualization of specially designed endovascular devices by utilizing laser light instead of fluoroscopy. These devices facilitate real-time visualization with three-dimensional features to simplify endovascular navigation without the necessity of using fluoroscopy during navigation. This is the first single-center study that presents an overview of 31 peripheral arterial disease (PAD) lesions (in 22 patients) showing that using FORS guided navigation in PAD interventions is safe and feasible. Ultimately, the use of FORS in combination with other radiation reducing technologies might eventually enable a radiation-free interventional environment in the future.

title: The 12 and 24 Months Results of the VMI-CFA Study, a Physician-Initiated Trial Investigating the Efficacy of the Vascular Mimetic Implant Supera Peripheral Stent System for the Treatment of the Common Femoral Artery.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The objective of the Vascular Mimetic Implant-Common Femoral Artery Study (VMI-CFA) investigation is to evaluate the mid-term (24 months) outcome of treatment of the common femoral artery (CFA) with the Supera Peripheral Stent System (Abbott Vascular Inc., Santa Clara, USA) in symptomatic (Rutherford 2-4), de novo stenotic or occlusive lesions. METHODS: One hundred patients with atherosclerotic lesions in the CFA were recruited for the VMI-CFA trial during routine consultations in hospitals in Belgium and France. The key inclusion criterion was de novo, stenotic (>50%) or occlusive lesions located in the native CFA. The main exclusion criteria were asymptomatic disease, (in-stent) restenosis and occlusion of the deep femoral artery. The primary efficacy and safety endpoint were defined respectively as primary patency at 12 months core lab adjudicated and any periprocedural adverse events up to 30 days post-procedure. The secondary endpoints included technical success rate, primary patency at 1, 6 and 24 months post-procedure, freedom from target lesion revascularization (TLR) at 1, 6, 12 and 24 months post-procedure and clinical success. RESULTS: The Supera Stent was deployed and implanted successfully in all 100 patients. At 12 and 24 months, the primary patency rate was 95.2% and 92.8%, respectively. Two patients had to undergo a TLR between 6 and 12 months of follow-up, which resulted in a freedom from TLR rate of 97.8%. This rate remained the same at 24-month follow-up. Regarding the primary safety endpoint, there were 17 periprocedural adverse events in the first month after the index procedure, but no device- or procedure-related deaths, TLRs, major target limb amputations or thromboses were reported. Survival rate at 12 months was 91.8%. At 1, 6 and 24 months of follow-up, the survival rate was 100%, 96.9% and 85.5%, respectively. Fourteen patients died during the 2-year follow-up period. None of the deaths was procedure- or study-device related. A clear shift from Rutherford classification 2 to 4 toward 0 to 1 was seen and displays the clinical success of the endovascular therapy with the Supera Peripheral Stent System. CONCLUSION: The VMI-CFA trial shows that endovascular treatment of the "no-stent zone" CFA atherosclerotic disease with the Supera Peripheral Stent System is a safe and efficient therapy in CFA treatment.Clinical ImpactThis study provides prospective evidence supporting Supera stenting for common femoral artery disease, traditionally treated by open endarterectomy. The encouraging patency and safety outcomes suggest a minimally invasive alternative for selected patients, particularly those with hostile groin anatomy or increased risk of wound complications. By specifically evaluating an interwoven nitinol stent in this challenging arterial territory, these findings may help clinicians individualize revascularization strategies. However, the nonrandomized design does not establish superiority over endarterectomy. Randomized comparative evidence is needed before broader adoption or changes to the current standard of care.

METHODS: One hundred patients with atherosclerotic lesions in the CFA were recruited for the VMI-CFA trial during routine consultations in hospitals in Belgium and France. The key inclusion criterion was de novo, stenotic (>50%) or occlusive lesions located in the native CFA.

title: Factors Associated With Primary Patency Loss After Covered Endovascular Reconstruction of the Aortic Bifurcation for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: An Individual Patient Data Meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Covered endovascular reconstruction of the aortic bifurcation (CERAB) has emerged as an endovascular treatment option for complex aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD). However, factors associated with loss of patency remain insufficiently defined. This individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis evaluated outcomes after CERAB and identified factors associated with loss of primary patency. METHODS: Six retrospective CERAB datasets including 412 patients treated for symptomatic AIOD between 2009 and 2021 were identified through systematic literature review, harmonized, and merged. The primary outcome was loss of primary patency. Secondary outcomes included primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, freedom from target lesion revascularization, morbidity, mortality, and functional outcomes. Kaplan-Meier analysis estimated patency and survival, while Cox proportional hazards regression identified factors independently associated with primary patency loss. RESULTS: P P P Technical success was achieved in 405/412 procedures (98.3%). Primary patency was 90.9% at 1 year and 76.8% at 5 years, whereas secondary patency remained greater than 95% throughout follow-up. Factors independently associated with loss of primary patency were younger age (hazard ratio [HR], 0.96/year; < .001), Rutherford category 4 to 6 (HR, 2.06, = .034), and prior target-area revascularization (HR, 2.44; = .006). Freedom from target lesion revascularization was 91.8% at 1 year and 80.1% at 5 years. Perioperative complications occurred in 10.4% of patients, and 30-day mortality was 1.0%. Ankle-brachial index and Rutherford classification improved significantly within 30 days, although long-term functional follow-up was limited by incomplete data. CONCLUSIONS: Covered endovascular reconstruction of the aortic bifurcation was associated with favorable mid-term patency, low perioperative morbidity, and meaningful early clinical improvement in patients with complex AIOD. Younger age, advanced Rutherford category, and prior target-area revascularization were independently associated with loss of primary patency.Clinical ImpactThis individual participant data meta-analysis moves beyond descriptive outcome reporting by identifying clinically relevant factors associated with patency loss after covered endovascular reconstruction of the aortic bifurcation for aortoiliac occlusive disease. It identifies younger age, advanced Rutherford stage, and previous target-area revascularization as factors associated with loss of primary patency. These findings add granularity to the existing CERAB literature and may help refine patient selection, inform counseling, and support more individualized follow-up strategies.

However, factors associated with loss of patency remain insufficiently defined. This individual patient data (IPD) meta-analysis evaluated outcomes after CERAB and identified factors associated with loss of primary patency.

title: Sequential decision-making in endovascular stroke therapy: benefit and harm of the next retrieval attempt after failed reperfusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: After failed reperfusion in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), interventionalists must outweigh the expected benefit of an additional retrieval attempt with the outcome of the current angiographic result. Framing EVT as an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem, the present study provides a per-pass evaluation of the expected benefit of EVT continuation versus procedural termination after unsuccessful reperfusion, based on large-scale real-world registry data. METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened. Inclusion criteria were (1) age ≥ 18 years, (2) anterior circulation LVO, (3) 1-15 retrieval attempts and (4) availability of relevant clinical data. Primary endpoint was the rate of good functional outcome, defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-2 at 90 days. For each retrieval attempt, patients were stratified into successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) and persistent occlusion (mTICI 0-2a). The net expected benefit of EVT continuation, Δ(k), was defined as the difference between the mRS 0-2 rate at pass k + 1, and the mRS 0-2 rate for unsuccessful reperfusion at pass k. A positive Δ(k) indicates that continuation is favored at that decision node k. The pass at which Δ(k) first becomes non-significant identifies the empirical, optimal stopping threshold. RESULTS: Among 9,495 included patients, successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) was achieved in 8,405 (89%), and 3,428 (36%) achieved good functional outcome at 90 days. Up to six retrieval attempts, Δ(k) was positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), indicating that continuation of EVT was associated with superior expected outcome at each of these decision points. At pass seven, Δ(k) became negative and lost statistical significance (p = 0.53), identifying this as the empirical optimal stopping threshold. CONCLUSION: Continuation of EVT up to six retrieval attempts confers a significant functional benefit over termination after unsuccessful reperfusion. These findings provide a decision-theoretic basis for individualized intraprocedural decision-making and suggest that functional independence can be achieved beyond conventionally assumed pass thresholds.

METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened.

title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization. OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies. METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals.

title: JTH in Clinic: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis of Pediatric Patients at Risk of VTE.
abstract: As the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) increases in hospitalized children, there is an urgent need to improve VTE prevention strategies in this population. Implementation of thromboprophylaxis, which includes mechanical and pharmacological interventions, varies in practice due to limited pediatric-specific data and, until recently, a lack of evidence-based guidelines. However, recent randomized clinical trials and well-designed multicenter observational studies have provided improved evidence on the safety and efficacy of anticoagulants for VTE prevention in specific pediatric subpopulations supporting the development of risk assessment models to help identify subgroups of children at high risk for VTE. Based on these data, the American Society of Hematology and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis recently developed the first evidence-based guideline for anticoagulant prophylaxis in children at risk of VTE. While this guideline is an exciting step towards preventing VTE-associated harm, VTE prevention remains complex due to unique pediatric risk factors and changing physiology with age, resulting in heterogeneous VTE and bleeding risk profiles. In this case-based review, we apply the new guideline and supporting evidence to guide decisions regarding the use of thromboprophylaxis in pediatric cases commonly encountered in clinical practice, highlighting the nuances of VTE prevention in critically ill children. We review the complex decision-making process required prior to initiation of pharmacologic prophylaxis, including assessment of VTE risk, bleeding risk, and shared decision-making with families. Additionally, we highlight the importance of multidisciplinary teams in VTE prevention and anticoagulant stewardship, as well as the similarities and differences in pediatric versus adult practice.

title: Update of a Living Network Meta-Analysis Comparing Non-compounded Polidocanol 1% Endovenous Microfoam (Varithena) Ablation versus Endovenous Thermal Ablation in Chronic Venous Insufficiency.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured polidocanol 1% endovenous microfoam and endovenous thermal ablation for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when polidocanol endovenous microfoam was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference. RESULTS: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). Polidocanol endovenous microfoam was not statistically different from endovenous thermal ablation for vein closure (odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.42 to 1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean 28 months, range 12-72 months) showed similar results (odds ratio 0.71, 95% confidence interval 0.45 to 1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with polidocanol endovenous microfoam versus endovenous thermal ablation (odds ratio 0.83, 95% confidence interval 0.29 to 2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific quality of life or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between polidocanol endovenous microfoam and endovenous thermal ablation (standardized mean difference [Hedges' g] 0.04, 95% confidence interval -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference. CONCLUSIONS: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that polidocanol 1% endovenous microfoam is not statistically different from endovenous thermal ablation for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation and endovenous thermal ablation for a composite of disease-specific quality of life and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.

This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of polidocanol endovenous microfoam ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026.

title: Snapshots of ATP-driven substrate translocation by the mitochondrial AAA+ protease AFG3L2.
abstract: AFG3L2, located in the mitochondrial inner membrane, is an ATP-fueled protease responsible for protein degradation, and its dysfunction has been implicated in multiple neurodegenerative disorders. However, the structural basis underlying its ATP-driven substrate translocation remains incompletely understood. Here, we purified full-length human AFG3L2 and determined its cryo-EM structures in four distinct conformational states (Con1-Con4), revealing substrate engagement in the core catalytic domain despite weak EM density for its transmembrane domain. These structures display an asymmetric spiral-staircase architecture in which the six protomers are arranged around a central pore that accommodates a polypeptide substrate. The four conformational states jointly reveal a substrate translocation mechanism in which ATP binding by the uppermost protomer promotes substrate engagement, whereas ATP hydrolysis by the lowermost ATP-bound protomer leads to substrate release. Our findings provide snapshots of ATP-driven substrate translocation by AFG3L2 and refine the hand-over-hand translocation mechanism by revealing substrate capture and release during an ordered ATPase cycle.

title: Association of Completion Imaging Modalities and Carotid Endarterectomy Outcomes in the Vascular Quality Initiative.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Completion imaging after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) confirms technical success and identifies defects requiring correction. However, the comparative effectiveness of imaging modalities in detecting clinically significant problems remains unclear. This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes. METHODS: CEAs performed between 2012-2024 in the VQI were analyzed. Completion imaging was categorized as none, Doppler, duplex ultrasound, or angiography. Intraoperative re-exploration rates were compared across modalities to assess detection of technical defects requiring revision. Postoperative outcomes were analyzed among patients who required re-exploration. Inverse probability weighted (IPW) logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios. Temporal trends were also analyzed. RESULTS: Among 208,786 CEAs, 24% had no completion imaging, 48% used Doppler, 24% duplex, and 4% angiography. Angiography had the highest intraoperative re-exploration rate (none 0.9%, doppler 0.9%, duplex 2.3%, angiography 3.6%; p<0.001). Among the 2,723 patients who required re-exploration, postoperative stroke occurred in 8.3% with no imaging, 12.5% with doppler, 3.7% with duplex, and 22.5% with angiography (p<0.001). In IPW-adjusted analyses, intraoperative duplex was associated with significant reduction in postoperative stroke compared to: no imaging (aOR 0.43, 95%CI 0.27-0.69), doppler (aOR 0.28, 95%CI 0.19-0.40), and angiography (aOR 0.13, 95%CI 0.09-0.20), all p<0.001. Overall, Angiography had the worst stroke outcomes. Doppler and angiography performed worse than duplex across additional endpoints, including ipsilateral stroke, TIA, any neurological event, return to OR, and 30-day mortality. Despite the stronger safety profile of duplex, it remains underused, as most CEAs performed in the last 15 years have utilized doppler or no imaging. CONCLUSIONS: Re-exploration and stroke outcomes after completion imaging reflect each modality's safety and efficacy in detecting significant technical defects. Duplex ultrasound demonstrated the lowest stroke rates and overall complications compared with angiography, doppler, and no imaging, suggesting its superior efficacy and safety. Doppler showed intermediate performance, while angiography carried the highest risk among patients who required re-exploration. Despite strong evidence favoring duplex, the majority of surgeons performing CEAs still rely on doppler or omit any completion imaging. Greater use of duplex ultrasound and incorporation of intraoperative duplex assessment into vascular training may improve intraoperative assessment, although further prospective evaluation is warranted.

However, the comparative effectiveness of imaging modalities in detecting clinically significant problems remains unclear. This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes.

title: Dynamic Infrared Thermography for Quantitative Assessment of Peripheral Microcirculation: Models, Metrics, and Clinical Translation.
abstract: Peripheral microcirculation assessment is critical for understanding tissue oxygenation, thermoregulation and metabolic function, but conventional techniques such as laser Doppler perfusion imaging and indocyanine green angiography are constrained by contact requirements, invasiveness or limited field of view. Dynamic infrared thermography (DIRT) provides a non-contact method that quantifies microvascular function by analyzing skin temperature recovery following a controlled thermal challenge, thereby offering functional insights into perfusion dynamics beyond static anatomical imaging. This narrative review synthesizes the bioheat models, quantitative metrics and clinical evidence supporting DIRT for peripheral microcirculation assessment. Following PRISMA-adapted searches, 71 studies and key modelling papers with dynamic protocols and perfusion-related quantitative endpoints were included. Bioheat transfer models, from the Pennes formulation to non-Fourier dual-phase-lag extensions, enable inverse estimation of perfusion parameters from temperature time-series. Validated metrics include rewarming rate, thermal time constant, area under the temperature vs time curve, maximum recovery percentage and spatial hotspot detection for perforator mapping. These parameters correlate strongly with laser Doppler and laser speckle contrast imaging, particularly in Raynaud's phenomenon, and achieve high diagnostic performance for preoperative perforator mapping and postoperative flap monitoring in reconstructive microsurgery. Evidence is most mature in surgical applications, supporting DIRT as a repeatable adjunct for planning and surveillance. In Raynaud's phenomenon, peripheral arterial disease and diabetic foot disease, DIRT metrics detect microvascular impairment and show promise for early ulceration risk prediction, although heterogeneity in protocols and scarcity of large-scale outcome data hinder broader adoption. As a conclusion, DIRT offers practical advantages of portability, negligible consumable cost and absence of contrast or ionizing radiation. Its transition to routine quantitative clinical use requires standardized acquisition protocols, integration of advanced signal processing and machine learning, and adequately powered multicenter trials linking metrics to patient-centered outcomes across populations.

title: Dose-Reduced Apixaban for Thromboembolism in a Patient With Obesity on Cobicistat: A Case Report.
abstract: Background/Objective: Summary: Conclusion: 2 2 2 2 Current guidelines recommend a 50% dose reduction of apixaban for patients receiving strong CYP3A4/P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibitors regardless of body habitus. However, evidence supporting this dose adjustment in patients with severe obesity (BMI >40 kg/m) is limited. This report describes the use of dose-reduced apixaban for the treatment of venous thromboembolism in a patient with a BMI >50 kg/mreceiving a strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitor.A 38-year-old female with a BMI of 81.71 kg/mand a history of HIV on a cobicistat-containing antiretroviral regimen was diagnosed with a left femoral deep vein thromboembolism. She was initially treated with warfarin and enoxaparin bridge therapy but was transitioned to apixaban prior to discharge. Apixaban was initiated at a 50% dose reduction due to the concomitant use of cobicistat, a strong CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitor. title: Sacral spinal dural arteriovenous fistula: diagnostic pitfalls and treatment challenges. Illustrative case.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sacral spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (sDAVFs) are rare and easily missed on imaging, especially when supplied by internal iliac branches. Regional vascular anatomy may complicate endovascular treatment approaches. OBSERVATIONS: A 71-year-old man with symptoms suggestive of spinal myelopathy underwent spinal MRI, which revealed multisegment T2 cord hyperintensity from T7 to L1 without serpiginous flow voids; spinal MR angiography (MRA) findings were negative for sDAVF. On spinal digital subtraction angiography (DSA), selective internal iliac injection identified a right S1 sDAVF originating from a lateral sacral artery branch. Transarterial Onyx embolization formed a plug proximal to the fistula, resulting in failed obliteration. Subsequent microsurgical disconnection via S1 laminectomy appeared successful on intraoperative ICG angiography, but postoperative angiography revealed residual shunting. Reexploration with L5 laminectomy allowed definitive microsurgical ligation, resulting in lasting cure at the 1-year follow-up. LESSONS: Negative spinal MRI/MRA findings do not rule out sacral sDAVF; complete spinal DSA, including internal iliac injection, is critical if sacral sDAVF is suspected. Sacral angioarchitecture may hinder durable embolization, warranting consideration of upfront microsurgical ligation. With ligation, intraoperative ICG angiography may miss residual flow; immediate postoperative angiography should be best practice. With microsurgical ligation, broad exposures may be ideal for identifying all arterialized veins. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26220.

title: From structural repair to biomechanical compatibility: Aortic stiffness after open and endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: Evaluation of aortic repair has traditionally prioritised perioperative safety, exclusion of the diseased segment and durability. As endovascular treatment expands to younger patients, attention is turning towards the biomechanical compatibility of prosthetic grafts with the native aorta. Native aortic compliance supports Windkessel function, whereas grafts create a compliance transition that may accelerate pulse-wave transmission, alter wave reflection and increase left-ventricular load. This narrative review distinguishes established evidence from emerging concepts after open surgical repair, endovascular aneurysm repair and thoracic endovascular aortic repair. Carotid-femoral pulse-wave velocity (cfPWV) is the accepted reference non-invasive measure of regional aortic stiffness; cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR)-derived segmental pulse-wave velocity and distensibility provide complementary information. Brachial-ankle pulse-wave velocity, the cardio-ankle vascular index, and augmentation index assess different territories or haemodynamic properties and are not interchangeable with cfPWV. Left-ventricular strain and mass are downstream cardiac outcomes. Clinical evidence generally reports increases in measured arterial-stiffness indices after endovascular repair, whereas findings after open repair are heterogeneous. Treatment length, landing-zone location, oversizing, anatomy and baseline vascular phenotype may be as important as graft fabric or stent-frame category. Conflicting comparisons of polyester and expanded polytetrafluoroethylene arise from small, non-randomised studies using non-equivalent endpoints and do not support a reliable ranking of commercial devices. Emerging 4D-flow CMR, simulation and compliant graft materials illustrate a shift from structural exclusion alone towards compliance-aware repair, but evidence of improved outcomes remains insufficient. Future studies should use standardised longitudinal stiffness, blood-pressure and cardiac assessments and relate biomechanical changes to hypertension, ventricular remodelling and cardiovascular outcomes.

title: Intracardiac thrombus and multiple venous thromboses revealing focal segmental glomerulosclerosis.
abstract: Nephrotic syndrome is associated with a hypercoagulable state, leading to an increased risk of potentially severe thromboembolic events. Although venous thromboses predominantly involve the renal veins and deep veins of the lower extremities, intracardiac thrombosis remains an exceptionally rare manifestation, particularly as the initial presenting feature. We report the case of a 51-year-old woman with a history of schizophrenia and recent cholecystectomy, who was admitted for lower-limb edema and hematuria of two weeks' duration. Computed tomography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis revealed multiple thrombotic events, including deep vein thrombosis of the lower extremities, partial thrombosis of the left renal vein, and a left ventricular intracardiac thrombus measuring 23 × 20 mm. Laboratory investigations demonstrated nephrotic syndrome with a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 10 g/g and hypoalbuminemia of 23 g/L, associated with stage 2 acute kidney injury. Immunological testing was negative, including anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA) and anti-phospholipase A2 receptor (anti-PLA2R) antibodies. Kidney biopsy established the diagnosis of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. Management consisted of therapeutic anticoagulation, diuretic therapy, and corticosteroid treatment, resulting in progressive clinical and biological improvement. This case highlights the exceptional occurrence of a left ventricular thrombus associated with multiple venous thromboses as the presenting manifestation of focal segmental glomerulosclerosis. It underscores the importance of systematically investigating underlying glomerular disease in patients presenting with multiple or unusual thrombotic events, particularly in the presence of significant proteinuria.

title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Kidney Transplant Recipients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant recipients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) may be at higher risk of venous thromboembolism than non-ADPKD recipients. METHODS: We conducted an observational study of adult kidney transplant recipients at a single center, the University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG; n=1179, 393 with ADPKD), and replicated key analyses in the multicenter Swiss Transplant Cohort Study (STCS; n=4415, 710 with ADPKD). The primary endpoint was time to first venous thromboembolism after transplantation or death related to venous thromboembolism (identified through medical record review), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression. Data were pooled for subgroup analyses and to assess determinants of post-transplant venous thromboembolism risk. RESULTS: Venous thromboembolism occurred more often in ADPKD than non-ADPKD kidney transplant recipients (log-rank p=0.04 and p<0.001 for UMCG and STCS, respectively). The 10-year cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 13.5% [95% CI: 9.4, 17.5], versus 9.6% [95% CI: 7.0, 12.1] in ADPKD versus non-ADPKD recipients in UMCG, and 21.0% [95% CI: 17.0, 24.7] versus 15.1% [95% CI: 13.5, 16.6] in STCS. Median [Q1, Q3] time to venous thromboembolism were similar across cohorts (UMCG: 1.7 [0.4, 4.9], STCS: 1.4 [0.2, 4.8] years). Venous thromboembolism risk was highest in the early (<2 years) post-transplant period. After adjustment for venous thromboembolism risk factors, ADPKD remained independently associated with post-transplant venous thromboembolism in both cohorts (UMCG HR 1.80 [95% CI: 1.21, 2.69]; STCS HR 1.39 [95% CI: 1.13, 1.72]). The association between ADPKD and risk of venous thromboembolism was more pronounced in males. Hemoglobin levels after kidney transplantation were approximately 7.0 ± 0.8% higher in ADPKD recipients, particularly in males, with corresponding higher risks of erythrocytosis during follow-up. Incorporating longitudinal hemoglobin as a time-varying covariate attenuated the association between ADPKD and venous thromboembolism, suggesting that the association was at least partially driven by higher hemoglobin levels. CONCLUSIONS: Kidney transplant recipients were at high risk for venous thromboembolism, and those with ADPKD are at an even higher risk.

title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
abstract: AIMS: Carotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. While current clinical guidelines for carotid endarterectomy rely primarily on stenosis severity and patient symptomatology, unstable plaques can cause strokes even with low to moderate stenosis, suggesting that factors beyond plaque stenosis may drive its instability. This study aimed to characterize the cellular and spatial features of plaque instability at both single-cell and subcellular resolution. METHODS AND RESULTS: single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on carotid endarterectomy samples from patients with clinically and histologically classified stable or unstable plaques, consisting of more than 53,000 cells. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophages, and T-lymphocytes accounted for ∼85% of plaque-resident cells, with unstable plaques showing increased abundance of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs, GZMK+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes, and antigen-presenting macrophages. In contrast, stable plaques were enriched in contractile and fibroblast-like VSMCs, alongside MRC1+ resident-like macrophages. To then spatially map these populations, CosMx™ high-plex spatial transcriptomics was integrated utilizing the unprecedented whole-transcriptome (∼18,934 targets) Human Discovery RNA panel. This revealed a distinct spatially disorganized plaque architecture in unstable plaques, characterized by infiltration of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs and effector T-lymphocytes distributed across both the fibrotic cap and lipid core, alongside distinct multicellular microenvironments enriched for adaptive immune engagement. This was in contrast to stable plaques, which exhibited more structured, macrophage-dominant spatial microenvironments and neighborhoods. We lastly profiled ∼90,000 paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to assess the plaque macroenvironment. PBMCs surrounding unstable plaques displayed exclusive enrichment of CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes and effector T-lymphocytes, which were depleted surrounding stable plaques. Ligand-receptor interaction analyses within CCL and CXCL-mediated pathways revealed enhanced immune-stromal signaling between PBMC-derived monocytes and plaque-resident VSMCs in the unstable plaque group, with coordinated chemokine-driven interactions indicating a shift toward VSMC- and T-lymphocyte mediated recruitment of circulating immune cells. CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate that carotid plaque instability is driven by spatially coordinated expansion of inflammatory VSMCs and effector immune cells within the plaque and from the circulation, with a shift from predominantly innate immune-dominant characteristics in stable plaques toward adaptive immune-enriched responses in unstable conditions. This integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approach refines an integrated immune-stromal framework linking local plaque remodeling with systemic immune activation, highlighting key tissue-resident and circulating contributors to instability and establishing a foundation for mechanism-informed diagnostics and targeted therapeutic strategies beyond stenosis severity.

title: Preoperative statin exposure and postoperative outcomes after primary shoulder arthroplasty: a propensity-matched analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Statin use is associated with reduced incidence of periprosthetic fracture and revision surgery following total hip and knee arthroplasty, but whether a similar relationship exists for shoulder arthroplasty remains unclear. The objective of this study was to evaluate the association between preoperative statin exposure and both short- and long-term complications following primary shoulder arthroplasty. METHODS: The TriNetX Research Network was used to identify patients who underwent primary total shoulder arthroplasty or shoulder hemiarthroplasty; they were separated into groups according to presence or absence of at least one statin prescription issued within the 3 months prior to surgery. Primary outcomes assessed included periprosthetic fracture and revision surgery using Kaplan-Meier survival analysis within 2 and 5 years. RESULTS: A total of 21,346 matched pairs were included. Rates of periprosthetic fracture and revision surgery were similar within 2 years. The 5-year incidence of revision surgery was minimally elevated in the statin-exposed cohort (hazard ratio, 1.096; 95% CI, 1.002-1.198), whereas 5-year survival was improved among statin users according to post hoc analysis (hazard ratio, 0.915; 95% CI, 0.846-0.990). Statin use was associated with increased risk of venous thromboembolism, hemorrhagic anemia, transfusion, and all-cause readmission within 90 days postoperatively (P<0.05). CONCLUSIONS: No relationship between preoperative statin use and periprosthetic fracture following primary shoulder arthroplasty was observed. However, statin therapy did correlate with minimally increased risk of revision surgery within 5 years, which may be more reflective of improved patient survival than true implant failure. Level of evidence: III.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery.
abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor's spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4's groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

title: The retrieved venous thrombus as a translational platform: a methodologic roadmap for venous immunothrombosis.
abstract: Percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy is now widely used for iliofemoral deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) across several device platforms, and every procedure yields intact human thrombus that is routinely discarded. Whether this material can be developed into a translational resource linking thrombus biology to clinical outcome has not been systematically addressed. A narrative, non-systematic review was performed. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched (January 2010 to August 2026) for studies addressing the biology, histopathology and translational analysis of mechanically retrieved venous thrombi, supplemented by reference-list, trial-registry and congress hand-searching. Published venous series remain small and largely confined to descriptive histology, disconnected from longitudinal outcomes. Intra-thrombus biology could address venous-specific questions that peripheral biomarkers and imaging alone cannot: post-thrombotic syndrome, incomplete recanalization, chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension and cancer-associated thrombosis. A device-agnostic framework is proposed, comprising structured intra-procedural sampling at the level of the case rather than the anatomical region, centralized specimen processing under harmonized quality standards, a tiered analytic pipeline anchored on quantitative immunohistochemistry, paired peripheral-biomarker collection, pre-specified hypotheses with feasibility-based sample sizes, and biobank infrastructure embedded in existing trial platforms. The equivalent programme in arterial thrombectomy supplies transferable methodology, subject to explicit boundary conditions. The retrieved venous thrombus is among the more underused translational specimens in vascular medicine. A standardized, registry-embedded characterization framework could accelerate progress toward precision venous thrombosis medicine.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression. RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

title: Short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) in children represents a significant and growing global health burden. This study aims to report the short- and mid-term outcomes of hemodialysis vascular access in pediatric patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted to assess outcomes in pediatric patients with various types of hemodialysis access. This prospective cohort study included all consecutive pediatric patients with ESRD who presented to the Vascular and Endovascular Surgery Department at a tertiary hospital from October 2022 to October 2023. RESULTS: The study included 50 pediatric patients, with a mean age of 10.5 ± 5.7 years. The cohort was predominantly female 35 (70%), while males accounted for 15 (30%) The overall technical success rate remained high at 45 (90%). The failure rate was 5 (10%). CONCLUSION: Our findings demonstrate that pediatric arteriovenous fistulas (predominantly autogenous), when carefully planned and executed, can achieve high primary success and patency rates, with manageable complications in children with end-stage renal disease.
